data.narrative:
Fuse Energy, a Series A nuclear energy company founded by JC Btaiche, is evaluated against a sector comp set of 11 total peers—3 public (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private firms including Helion, Oklo, Valar Atomics, X-Energy, and Nano Nuclear Energy. The company has raised $78M to date and carries a last post-money valuation of $200M+.

Stage-progression analysis proves the only applicable quantitative method. A 2.0x multiplier applied to the $200M Series A post-money yields an implied forward valuation of $400M, consistent with observed step-up patterns at the Series A-to-B transition in the sector. Peer-median triangulation was not executable: while 5 same-sector peers exist, none of the tighter filter cohorts (same-stage, adjacent-stage, or valuation-tier comparable) contained the minimum 3 datapoints required for statistical relevance; broader peer aggregation would introduce unacceptable noise.

The triangulated valuation range is $340M (low) to $460M (high), with a median of $400M. This narrow band reflects reliance on a single method rather than cross-validation across multiple approaches. Key uncertainties include the absence of same-stage peer comps—rendering the stage-progression step-up assumption unvalidated against direct market evidence—and the wide dispersion likely present within the small private peer universe. Refinement would require disclosure of recent comparables' financials or expanded transaction precedent data.
